purpose: GENERATION-3 DIFFICULTY FIXTURE. Both prior families saturated: a frontier model one-shots a well-specified single-file ticket. Difficulty hypothesis from our own data: one-shot breaks on a LARGE, UNDER-specified behavioural surface. This fixture replays a real FOUR-COMMIT era on VextrumFrontend's edition renderer (3c8af98 'fixes to reports' -> 778c755 'vector chart and others' -> 707587c 'better report formatting' -> 225e1ef 'citation fixes'; ~470 churn on one module): the before-state renders trend/multi-line charts as text dumps, the after-state draws real vector charts, plus block-citation, formatting, ordering and citation-hygiene changes. The grader is MECHANICAL (build_era_oracle.py derives predicates from the era diff over a rich corpus, altformat-filtered) and the v2 stub records DRAWING as well as text, in emission order. PER-FAMILY PROJECTION POLICY keeps every graded expectation implementation-agnostic (kindset for charts, textseq for text, count for citation runs); era changes that live only in draw-event details (bars/ratio/fallback layout, sources, gaps) are DROPPED from grading and NAMED as unverified dimensions rather than silently absorbed — the measured over-constraint lesson applied to grader design.

local_source.normalization_note: None needed (verified in v1 and by the era derivation probe): zero top-level imports; jspdf resolves to the fixture stub, editionPdfAssets is optional behind try/catch. The driver uses the era's STABLE public surface (buildEditionDoc || downloadEditionPdf): buildEditionDoc was born DURING the era.
local_source.altformat_note: The middot separator variant (valid-but-different): kills separator-identity pinning at derivation time and proves grader format-agnosticism at admission time.

grading_surface.api: downloadEditionPdf(edition, meta) — the entry point present at every era ref (buildEditionDoc, when present, is preferred by the driver)
grading_surface.recording_stub: public/node_modules/jspdf/index.mjs v2: one `events` stream, text AND drawing in emission order; coordinates rounded to integers by the stub itself so no predicate can pin float layout
grading_surface.mechanical_grader: hidden/grade.py executes hidden/derived-predicates.json (16 predicates: 11 discriminating + 5 preservation guards, 7 families). Hand-made parts: the corpus, the family grouping and the projection policy; every expectation VALUE is mechanical.

convention_anchors.quote: Trend and multi-line visuals are drawn as real vector charts
A table visual renders its column headers and every row's cells
A citation must not be rendered twice in the same run.
At most three citations are rendered in a run.
Citations in a run are visually separated

A block's own `citations` list renders beneath that block as its numbered
  source references.

the marker
  style the source happened to use must not survive into the deliverable as
  literal text.
Blocks and visuals interleave strictly by their declared `order` key.
Cleaning up how content is presented must never delete what it says.

expected_controls.note: The REAL pre-era module: passes only preserved-behaviour (its own pinned text on the unchanged surface), fails all six change families. Measured deterministic score 14.

campaign_loop_overrides.reason: Same rationale as vextrum-v1/hermes-etl (measured binding at 30 on v1); the era task is 4x wider, so the raised budget keeps the measured axis the work, not the clock.

interpretation: Underspecified-by-design at scale: a symptom-level task plus discoverable conventions covering a ~470-churn four-commit rework. Every graded family is anchored to a CONVENTIONS.md sentence; five layout-level era changes are ungraded AND NAMED (ungraded_named_dimensions in the grader output) so green never quietly claims them. Score moves in steps of ~14 (7 families). HONEST CAVEATS to publish with any result: same module and repo as vextrum-v1 (this measures the DIFFICULTY axis, not family independence); citation-hygiene rides on a piece-count projection, which assumes the agent extends the module's existing emission granularity rather than rewriting it — a rewrite that changes granularity would fail that family for a debatable reason (flagged, not hidden).
